series.name: Technical Specifications
series.description: Captures hardware, software, performance, integration, and timeline constraints for the build.

open_ended.text: What hardware platforms or architectures must be supported? (CPU, GPU, mobile, embedded, etc.)

follow_up_choices.text: Single architecture — x86-64 desktop/server only
Dual architecture — e.g., x86-64 + ARM
Mobile/embedded — ARM, RISC-V, or specialized hardware
Platform-agnostic — must run on any reasonably modern hardware

open_ended.text: What are the minimum and recommended hardware specs? (RAM, storage, compute, network)

follow_up_choices.text: Minimal — <1GB RAM, <100MB storage, single-core sufficient
Standard — 2–8GB RAM, 1–10GB storage, multi-core recommended
High-performance — 16–64GB RAM, SSD storage, GPU recommended
Enterprise — 128GB+ RAM, distributed storage, multi-GPU clusters

open_ended.text: What bandwidth, latency, or networking requirements exist? Is offline operation needed?

follow_up_choices.text: Always-online — requires reliable internet connection
Online with offline fallback — core features work disconnected
Primarily offline — sync is optional or batch-oriented
Edge-deployed — must operate on intermittent or low-bandwidth connections

open_ended.text: What storage infrastructure is needed? (databases, object storage, caching, file systems)

follow_up_choices.text: Single database — one relational or document store covers all needs
Primary DB + cache — e.g., PostgreSQL with Redis
Polyglot persistence — multiple specialized data stores
Distributed storage — sharded databases, multi-region replication

open_ended.text: What cloud, on-premise, or hybrid infrastructure is targeted? Are there compliance or sovereignty requirements?

follow_up_choices.text: Cloud-native — designed for a specific cloud provider
Cloud-agnostic — portable across providers
On-premise only — deployed in private data centers
Hybrid — components span cloud and on-premise with strict compliance

open_ended.text: What programming languages, runtimes, or frameworks are required or preferred?

follow_up_choices.text: Single language — one ecosystem covers everything
Two languages — e.g., backend + frontend split
Polyglot — 3+ languages for specialized components
Language-agnostic — choice delegated to implementation team

open_ended.text: What operating systems and environments must be supported?

follow_up_choices.text: Linux only
Linux + macOS (developer-focused)
Cross-platform — Linux, macOS, Windows
Containerized — only targets Docker/K8s; host OS is irrelevant

open_ended.text: What existing libraries, services, APIs, or third-party dependencies should be used or avoided?

follow_up_choices.text: Minimal dependencies — build from standard library where possible
Core curated deps — choose established libraries for major concerns
Ecosystem-driven — leverage framework convention over custom code
Heavy integration — depend on multiple external services and SaaS

open_ended.text: What versioning, compatibility, or upgrade policies govern the software stack?

follow_up_choices.text: Latest-stable — always use current versions, update frequently
LTS-only — pinned to long-term support versions
Semver-constrained — explicit version ranges with CI verification
Locked — dependencies are vendored and updated on a release cycle

open_ended.text: What build systems, CI/CD platforms, and packaging formats are required?

follow_up_choices.text: Simple build — single build tool, manual or script-based deployment
CI-built — automated builds on push, artifact registry
Full CI/CD — automated testing, staging, and production deployment
GitOps — infrastructure-as-code with automated promotion pipelines

open_ended.text: What are the throughput, latency, and concurrency requirements? (requests/sec, response time, simultaneous users)

follow_up_choices.text: Low traffic — <100 req/s, seconds of latency, single-digit concurrency
Moderate traffic — 100–10K req/s, sub-second latency, hundreds concurrent
High traffic — 10K–100K req/s, low-latency targets, thousands concurrent
Internet scale — 100K+ req/s, strict SLOs, global distribution

open_ended.text: What data volume and growth rate is expected? (storage size, records, throughput)

follow_up_choices.text: Small — <10GB data, slow growth, single-node viable
Medium — 10GB–1TB, moderate growth, needs partitioning
Large — 1TB–100TB, rapid growth, requires distributed architecture
Massive — 100TB+, petabyte-scale, data lifecycle management needed

open_ended.text: What availability, uptime, and disaster recovery targets are required?

follow_up_choices.text: Best-effort — no formal SLA, occasional downtime acceptable
Standard — 99.9% uptime, daily backups, basic DR plan
High — 99.99% uptime, multi-region redundancy, automated failover
Critical — 99.999%+ uptime, active-active, zero-data-loss DR

open_ended.text: What scalability model is required? (vertical, horizontal, elastic, serverless)

follow_up_choices.text: Vertical — scale up a single node as needed
Horizontal — add/remove nodes with load balancer
Elastic — auto-scale based on metrics
Serverless — event-driven scale managed by platform

open_ended.text: What security and compliance standards must be met? (auth, encryption, audit, regulations)

follow_up_choices.text: Basic — password auth, TLS, no formal compliance requirements
Standard — OAuth2/MFA, encryption at rest, audit logging
Regulated — SOC2, HIPAA, GDPR, or PCI-DSS requirements
High-security — air-gapped, FIPS, zero-trust architecture

open_ended.text: What external systems, APIs, or services must this system integrate with?

follow_up_choices.text: No integrations — fully standalone system
1–2 integrations — limited surface area for interoperability
3–7 integrations — multiple external touchpoints
8+ integrations — integration-heavy, requiring an API gateway or ESB

open_ended.text: What integration protocols, data formats, or standards must be supported?

follow_up_choices.text: REST/JSON only — simple HTTP-based communication
REST + events — REST APIs plus message queue or event stream
gRPC + protobuf — type-safe, high-performance contracts
Multiple protocols — REST, gRPC, GraphQL, file-based, and binary formats

open_ended.text: What is the expected timeline, milestones, and delivery cadence?

follow_up_choices.text: Quick — prototype in weeks, production in 1–3 months
Standard — phased delivery over 3–9 months
Ambitious — 9–18 months with multiple major releases
Large program — 18+ months with distinct workstreams

open_ended.text: What testing, staging, and rollout strategy is required?

follow_up_choices.text: Basic — dev + production environments, manual testing
Standard — dev, staging, production with automated test suite
Robust — preview deployments, canary releases, feature flags
Enterprise — full deployment matrix, blue-green, chaos engineering

open_ended.text: What documentation, training, or knowledge transfer outputs are expected alongside the system?

follow_up_choices.text: Minimal — inline comments and a README
Standard — API docs, architecture decision records, setup guide
Comprehensive — full technical docs, runbooks, user manuals
Certification-level — training materials, compliance documentation, formal specs
